padaccheda: तम् । अथ । असौ । तथा । बुद्धि-फल-पल्लव-शालिनम् । आनन्द-मन्थर-मनाः । पुष्प-रूप-अचल-उपमम्
anvaya: अथ असौ आनन्द-मन्थर-मनाः तथा बुद्धि-फल-पल्लव-शालिनम् पुष्प-रूप-अचल-उपमम् तम् (कदम्बम् अपश्यत्) ।
meaning_english: Then, his mind slow with bliss, he beheld that Kadamba tree, which was adorned with the fruits and sprouts of wisdom and resembled a mountain made of flowers.

padaccheda: कदम्बम् । रोदसी-स्तम्भम् । आरुरोह । वन-स्थितम् । एक-अर्णव-गतम् । शौरिः । वट-वृक्षम् । इव । उन्नतम्
anvaya: (असौ) रोदसी-स्तम्भम् वन-स्थितम् उन्नतम् कदम्बम् (तथा) आरुरोह इव एक-अर्णव-गतम् वट-वृक्षम् शौरिः ।
meaning_english: He climbed that lofty Kadamba tree standing in the forest—a pillar between heaven and earth—just as Śauri (Viṣṇu) ascended the banyan tree amidst the single cosmic ocean.

content_sanskrit: तत्रासौ व्योमलग्नायाः शाखायाः प्रान्तपल्लवे । विवेश विगताशङ्कमेकाग्रं तप आस्थितः
padaccheda: तत्र । असौ । व्योम-लग्नायाः । शाखायाः । प्रान्त-पल्लवे । विवेश । विगताशङ्कम् । एकाग्रम् । तपः । आस्थितः
anvaya: असौ तत्र व्योम-लग्नायाः शाखायाः प्रान्त-पल्लवे विगताशङ्कम् विवेश (तथा) एकाग्रम् तपः आस्थितः (अभवत्) ।
meaning_english: There, upon the sprout at the very tip of a branch touching the sky, he entered fearlessly and remained established in one-pointed penance.

content_sanskrit: अथोपविश्य मृदुनि नवपल्लवविष्टरे । क्षणमालोकितास्तेन दिशः कौतुकचञ्चलम्
padaccheda: अथ । उपविश्य । मृदुनि । नव-पल्लव-विष्टरे । क्षणम् । आलोकिताः । तेन । दिशः । कौतुक-चञ्चलम्
anvaya: अथ मृदुनि नव-पल्लव-विष्टरे उपविश्य तेन क्षणम् कौतुक-चञ्चलम् दिशः आलोकिताः ।
meaning_english: Then, sitting upon a soft seat of fresh sprouts, he gazed for a moment at the various directions with eyes flickering in curiosity.
The directions appeared beautiful with necklaces of rivers, their breast-buds were the great mountains, the clear sky was their braided hair, and the moving dark clouds were their locks of hair.
Clad in garments of blue leaves, adorned with ear-ornaments of flower-clusters, they held the full pitchers of the oceans and were bedecked with many ornaments.
They held blossoming lotus-ponds, their breath was fragrant wind, they possessed the soft sounds of blue bees, and the tinkling of waterfalls served as their anklets.
With the heavens as their heads and the earth as their feet, the lines of forests were their body-hair; they had the jungles as thighs and hips, and the moon and sun served as their earrings.
They possessed fields of rice-crops, were accompanied by bowls of sandalwood paste, and wore the snow-white clouds as garments clinging to the breasts of mountain peaks.
The vast expanse of ocean waters served as their fresh decorative mirrors; they had horripilation in the form of the multitude of stars, appearing as the inner apartments of the universe.

The ten directions appeared like celestial women, adorned with the seasons as their breasts, smeared with the saffron of the sun's rays, decorated with various flowers, and anointed with the white sandalwood-paste of the moonbeams.

content_sanskrit: गगनगतलतादलोपविष्टः प्रसृतवनावनिवारिवाहवेषाः । त्रिभुवनवनिता ददर्श हृष्टः कुसुमनिरन्तरमण्डिता दशाशाः
padaccheda: गगन-गत-लता-दल-उपविष्टः । प्रसृत-वन-अवनि-वारिवाह-वेषाः । त्रि-भुवन-वनिताः । ददर्श । हृष्टः । कुसुम-निरन्तर-मण्डिताः । दश-आशाः
anvaya: (सः) हृष्टः गगन-गत-लता-दल-उपविष्टः प्रसृत-वन-अवनि-वारिवाह-वेषाः कुसुम-निरन्तर-मण्डिताः त्रि-भुवन-वनिताः दश-आशाः ददर्श ।
meaning_english: The joyful one beheld the ten directions, which appeared like the women of the three worlds; they were seated upon the leafy creepers of the sky, garbed in the clouds of the expansive forest-lands, and incessantly adorned with blossoms.
